This PR adds two new contracts: **`ServiceRegistry`** and **`PartnerConfiguration`**. Both of the contracts use ERC-7201 namespaced storage layout.

### **`ServiceRegistry`**

* This contract acts as a resolver for the service name and service name hashes. `SERVICE_REGISTRY_ADMIN_ROLE` members can register and unregister services.

* Service registry works by providing a string as a `serviceName` and the function hashes it using `keccak256` and adds the hash to a list, and adds name and hash to a two mappings. One for `hash > name`  and one for `name > hash`.

* This contract is inherited by the `CMAccountManager` contract. This means that the manager contract is the service name resolver.

### **`PartnerConfiguration`**

* This contract implements features like adding/removing supported services, setting fees and capabilities for each service. Adding a service first checks if the service hash is registered on the manager, if not, it reverts with `ServiceNotRegistered` error.

* Add/remove public keys, get all public keys from a CM Account.

* This contract is inherited by the `CMAccount` contract.

> [!TIP]
> Check out tests in the Github Actions for gas consumption

author: lindsaym-fa
body:
Adds a page with a thumbnail grid of all standalone Web Awesome components. The goal is to give WA users a better platform to browse WA component offerings, whereas the sidebar provides a scannable list effective for when users already have a specific component in mind.

I opted to exclude child components (wa-carousel-item, wa-breadcrumb-item, etc.) since these are discoverable through their parent components. (Users may not be as likely to have success discovering these by 'browsing.') 

Components are organized into categories in the index but kept as a single, alphabetical list in the sidebar. This supports the distinct goals of each entry point: users looking for a specific component can scan the list predictably in alphabetical order without the barrier of having to guess its category, while users who are browsing to discover components in the index get an extra hint at each components' purpose.

Feedback appreciated. 😊

author: amandabirmingham
body:
There are a few things going on in this PR:
* Lots more replacement of string literals with constants. This makes up the largest bulk of individual changes, but (if done right ;) should make no changes to functionality.
* Change of control type string from `control_blank` to `control blank` in the test files since I misremembered what Gail is using in the standards doc.  This makes up the second largest bulk of changes, but is also pretty trivial.
* Rationalization of identification of blanks in `metapool` module: functions that are working with a plate df that contains a boolean `"Blanks"` column can use that to id blank samples. This helps wean us away from having every module and its mother individually doing string evaluations on sample names to identify blanks.
* More control-related functionality for extracting info from the sample context data frame, localized to `controls` module.
* More functionality for extracting project, sample, and control info from the sample sheet object, localized to the `sample_sheet` module.  The user(s) for these new public functions are outside this repo: they will be in `mg_scripts`' `sequence_processing_pipeline.CommitJob` (to get info needed to copy controls between projects) and in `qp-knight-lab-processing`'s `Step` (to identify non-blank samples without having to contents of sample names).
* Trivial change to how katharoseq tests compose the paths to their test files to bring them in line with other tests that can be run from any directory, not just the top directory of the repo.

This PR cleans and improves the implementation of `list`.
In particular:

1. kill `ListFactory`: thanks to support for metatypes, we can now implement the app-level `list` and the interp-level `W_List`, and use `W_List.meta_op_GETITEM` to allows things like `list[i32]`.

2. kill the ugly manual `CACHE`. Now that we support blue builtins, we can rely on  standard blue caching mechanism.
